high_risk_moment: Creator approves the AI-generated multi-language dub and publishes, but the pre-publish check fails to detect that the dub is realistic enough for viewers to mistake it for the creator's real recorded voice, so no synthetic-audio disclosure label is applied before the video goes live.
stakeholder: Viewers in the dubbed-language audience who cannot tell the audio is AI-generated
harm_description: Viewers reasonably believe they are hearing the creator's authentic voice when the audio is synthetically generated. SRC-01 documents that undisclosed AI voice/likeness synthesis of a known creator has already been used to deceive viewers into trusting a fraudulent offer, and SRC-04/SRC-06 show platforms and regulators now treat this exact disclosure gap as a compliance failure.
existing_controls: An automated policy-classification check runs before publish and is intended to catch missing disclosures, but its detection accuracy specifically for in-product AI-dubbed audio has not yet been evaluated.
proposed_controls: Treat every dub produced by the in-product voice-cloning feature as realistic-synthetic-audio by default (opt-out only with human policy-reviewer sign-off), auto-apply the platform's AI-generated-audio disclosure label, and run a quarterly precision/recall audit of the classifier against a held-out labeled test set.
human_oversight: A trust & safety reviewer is looped in only when the classifier flags a case; the reviewer sees the source video, the generated dub, and the classifier's confidence score, and has authority to hold or release the publish and to override the auto-label within the platform's published SLA before the video goes live.
monitoring_metric: Weekly-sampled audit precision/recall of the synthetic-audio disclosure classifier against a human-labeled test set
trigger_threshold: Recall on the audit set for realistic AI-dubbed audio falls below 95% OR any confirmed viewer-deception incident is reported
response_action: Pause auto-clear for that dub type, force human review on 100% of publishes until recall is restored above threshold, and notify affected creators and platform trust & safety.

high_risk_moment: The creator records a voice sample and sends it to the third-party voice-cloning vendor to generate the dub, and the product does not verify or contractually confirm what the vendor is allowed to do with that voice sample afterward.
stakeholder: The creator whose voice sample is submitted to the vendor for cloning
harm_description: If the voice-cloning vendor retains or reuses a creator's submitted voice sample beyond generating the requested dub, the creator's voice could be cloned and reused in content they never authorized. SRC-02 documents this happening to two voice actors whose samples were reportedly used beyond the stated internal-research purpose, leading to reported unauthorized reuse and lost income.
existing_controls: The vendor's standard terms of service govern data use; the product team has not independently verified or audited what the vendor does with submitted voice samples after the dub is generated.
proposed_controls: Add a contractual data-processing addendum requiring the vendor to delete or not reuse voice samples beyond the specific dub job, require an auditable deletion/no-reuse attestation from the vendor, and give creators an explicit, separate consent screen plus the ability to request deletion of their submitted voice sample.
human_oversight: Legal/privacy reviewer approves the vendor data-processing addendum before any vendor is onboarded, and a product/privacy owner reviews the vendor's deletion attestation on a recurring cadence; creators can escalate a suspected voice-misuse report, which routes to this reviewer for investigation with authority to suspend the vendor.
monitoring_metric: Vendor deletion/no-reuse attestation completion rate and count of creator-reported voice-misuse escalations
trigger_threshold: Vendor misses a quarterly attestation OR any single creator-reported voice-misuse escalation is confirmed
response_action: Suspend new voice-cloning jobs routed to that vendor pending investigation, notify affected creators, and require a corrective data-handling plan before resuming.
